To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

inhibition of arachidonic acid 5-lipo-oxygenase (5-LO) induces apoptosis of prostate cancer cells by activating death receptor-mediated signaling pathways and inhibiting the antiapoptotic protein survivin.
inhibition of the 5-LOX enzyme in prostate cancer cells induces cell death via Fas death receptor signaling pathway.
the inhibition of arachidonic acid metabolism by 5-lipoxy-genase inhibitor, zileuton, induces cell death in prostate cancer cells through the activation of Fas death signal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of cell death and survival in tumor cells.
the identification of new molecular targets that could be used for the design of new anticancer agents that would be more efficient and less toxic than those currently available.
the molecular mechanisms of cell death and survival in cancer and the development of therapeutic modalities to reverse the order by induction of cell death or inhibition of cell growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
apoptosis is the most effective way for cancer cells to die and the major determinant of the success of any cancer-therapy regimen.
cancer cells are highly resistant to apoptosis, which is the main reason behind the failure of current chemotherapeutic strategies to cure cancer patients.
the induction of apoptosis by a therapeutic modality would be the most efficient way to eliminate tumor cells without much side effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inhibition of 5-lipo-oxygenase (5-LO) in prostate cancer cells triggers cell death by apoptosis and that this process is mediated by Fas death receptor signaling pathway.
the arachidonate lipoxygenases (5-LO and 12-LO) are the key players in the regulation of the Fas death receptor pathway in prostate cancer cells.
we have discovered the molecular mechanisms of prostate cancer death induced by inhibition of the arachidonate lipoxygenase, 5-LOX, which is a key enzyme of leukotriene biosynthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 5-LO pathway is an important player in the regulation of apoptosis in cancer cells.
the 5-LO inhibitor is a potent inducer of apoptosis in prostate cancer cells, which is mediated by the activation of Fas death receptors.
the arachidonate lipoxygenase inhibitor is a potent inducer of apoptosis in prostate cancer cells, which may be exploited for therapeutic benefit.
